"A high-fidelity 3D open-world life simulator and crime RPG set across the entire San Francisco Bay Area. Starting broke at 18, the player navigates realistic living costs, survival needs, deep economic pathways, and criminal systems within a living urban sandbox.
 * World, Environment @COMMENT_BODY@ Physics:
   * Dynamic Microclimates: Bay Area weather simulation featuring dense marine fog, rainstorms, heatwaves, and seasonal shifts affecting visibility, tire traction, and heating costs.
   * RDR2-Style Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Physics: Weighted, momentum-based directional punches, kicks, blocks, grapples, dynamic hit reactions, and ragdoll physics.
   * Seamless Multi-City Map: Diverse districts across the Bay with realistic transit, traffic systems, and neighborhood-specific demographics.
 * Survival, Aging @COMMENT_BODY@ Living Systems:
   * Full Life Cycle: Dynamic aging system with visible physical changes, fitness levels, and a 28-day monthly calendar.
   * Vitals @COMMENT_BODY@ Maintenance: Hunger, thirst, hygiene, bladder/bowel, fatigue/bed quality, temperature/winter heating, and mental state.
   * Real Estate @COMMENT_BODY@ Assets: Renting, property ownership, interior decoration, mortgages, property taxes, vehicle purchases, maintenance, and gas consumption.
   * Lifestyle: Dating, marriage, pets, functional smartphones with apps, social networking, sports, gaming, and custom wardrobe.
 * Economy, Gig Work @COMMENT_BODY@ Entrepreneurship:
   * Flexible Hustles: App-based gig economy (rideshare, courier, package delivery) and entry-level hourly work.
   * Corporate Ladders: Dozens of career tracks (tech, medicine, legal, aerospace, politics, engineering, culinary, trades) with promotions and salary tiers.
   * Business Ownership: Buy, launch, and manage legitimate businesses, hire staff, handle supply chains, set profit margins, and launder illicit revenue.
 * Deep Criminal Hierarchy @COMMENT_BODY@ Law Enforcement:
   * Criminal Underworld: Progress from street-level pickpocketing, shoplifting, scams, and corner dealing to running drug labs, arms trafficking, high-stakes heists, loan sharking, and syndicate management.
   * Turf @COMMENT_BODY@ Street Heat: Gang wars, violent clashes with law enforcement, extortion, and district control.
   * Police @COMMENT_BODY@ Legal Consequences: Aggressive, tactically responsive police AI, warrants, vehicle pursuits, arrests, and randomized court trials.
   * Playable Open-World Prison: Seamless transfer to a high-security prison sandbox. Survive rival gangs, craft shivs, run prison hustles, manage yard politics, or coordinate escapes.
 * Interactive AI @COMMENT_BODY@ Character Systems:
   * Smart NPCs: Distinct personalities, memory of player actions, daily schedules, emotional states, and voice-acted/procedural dialogue trees.
   * Skill Tree: Action-driven skill advancement (stamina, driving, stealth, marksmanship, charisma, hacking) leveled up through active use.
   * Complete Customization: Deep character creator for appearance, body type, posture, voice, and traits.
* in depth gang hierarchy with the option to join any of the gangs with rivals and allies and a constant fight over turf and over criminal empires.

## Objective
- Finish and verify the playable Bay Area life-simulator game in `index.html`, covering core gameplay.
- Keep it immediately playable; summarize its scope and limitations when complete.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them at finish.
- Include needs, work/economy, districts, social and turf systems, law consequences, and aging/calendar.
- Keep criminal activities abstract RPG choices.

## Decisions
- Build a self-contained, stylized 2D overhead browser RPG.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core game UI and systems, including saving, travel, work, needs, housing, social actions, fictional crews, heat/custody, and calendar/aging.
- Improved the minimap to show connected district stops with a highlighted current district.
- Made work shifts advance the hours shown, added paid shifts for career roles, and corrected the weekly-rent day check.
- Confirmed the minimap canvas was drawing at a wide viewport; its previous rendering was hard to distinguish visually.

### Active
- Re-run JavaScript syntax validation and verify gameplay flows, persistence, career shifts, sleep timing, and rent timing in-browser.
- Polish any remaining issues before summarizing the 2D scope and limitations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run syntax validation and test the updated game in Chromium at a wide viewport.
2. Verify career shifts, rental timing, sleep-to-7:00-AM behavior, and save restoration.
3. Fix any remaining issues, then summarize what is playable and note the 2D scope assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is untracked in the current Git status.
- Earlier, `node --check /tmp/baybound.js` passed and `/usr/bin/chromium` rendered the game; recent edits have not yet been revalidated.
- The previous `playwright-cli` attempt could not run because its expected Chromium installation was missing.

- Transform Baybound from its current top-down 2D prototype into a third-person, over-the-shoulder open-world life simulator with touch controls, immersive 3D presentation, NPC interactions, and a vehicle-based starting safe house.

- Use a focused GTA V/RDR2-style camera with touch-drag control, tap-to-focus, and a translucent joystick that appears where touched and hides when released.

## Objective
- Convert Baybound’s top-down life-simulator prototype into a third-person, over-the-shoulder open-world game with touch controls, richer city simulation, NPC interactions, and a vehicle-based starting safe house.

## Requirements
- Retain the playable prototype while replacing its top-down perspective.
- Add drag-to-look and tap-to-focus camera controls, a touch joystick that appears at the touch point and hides on release, and contextual punch, grapple, dodge, and block buttons.
- Develop 3D buildings and interiors, living NPCs, clothing and animations, vehicles, lighting, reflections, ambient occlusion, shadows, and dynamic city events.
- Add NPC chatbot conversations and the requested street-drug and smoke-shop economy, paraphernalia, weapons, clothing, sales supplies, and concealment items.
- Start the player in a broken-down, insecure car with a stash trunk, sleeping backseat, radio, and charging outlet; repairs or replacement should cost time and money.
- The earlier request for “full nsfw capabilities” remains unscoped.

## Decisions
- Keep the existing playable prototype as the baseline.
- Use the existing Canvas renderer for an initial perspective-rendered city; full 3D rendering, asset pipeline, and chatbot approach remain undecided.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added touch pointer controls with a dynamic joystick, camera drag/tap-focus scaffolding, perspective projection, and a Canvas pseudo-3D city renderer in `index.html`.
- Added contextual combat controls near NPCs; punch/grapple affect trust and street heat, while dodge/block are stance practice.
- Syntax-checked the inline JavaScript successfully before the latest projection-basis edit.
- Browser-tested the page; the only console error observed was a missing `/favicon.ico`.

### Active
- Validate and refine the perspective renderer: the first browser screenshot showed the player and city geometry misprojected; the projection’s vertical-basis signs were corrected, but the result has not yet been recaptured.
- Verify keyboard movement, touch joystick, camera drag/tap focus, and interactions; the focus-hit depth threshold was corrected from `<40` to `<900`.

### Blocked
- High-fidelity 3D assets, interiors, animations, advanced lighting, and chatbot functionality are absent; implementation and service/asset choices remain unresolved.
- The vehicle-based safe house and economy/content systems remain unimplemented.

## Next Move
1. Recapture the browser after the projection-basis fix and confirm the player and buildings render correctly.
2. Test movement, camera drag/tap focus, touch joystick appearance/release, and NPC interactions; fix any issues.
3. Implement the vehicle-based starting safe house, then continue with simulation, NPC, and content systems incrementally.
